label: Bible Study
prompt: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in _____!
verse: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
note: A Song of Degrees for pilgrims headed to Jerusalem — brotherly harmony, compared to precious oil and mountain dew.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: He is not here: for he is _____, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
verse: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
note: The angel's Easter sermon is short: he is not here, he is risen, come and see. Best news ever preached.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not _____, but believing.
verse: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
note: The origin of 'doubting Thomas' — though the word Jesus actually uses in the KJV is faithless.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I have planted, Apollos _____; but God gave the increase.
verse: I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
note: Corinth was splitting into preacher fan clubs; Paul says preachers are just gardeners — the growth is all God's.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son _____ us from all sin.
verse: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
note: 'Cleanseth' is present tense in the Greek — it keeps on cleansing, not a one-time rinse.
